Question Choices: Define one radian using arc length and radius.
Question Answers: the angle subtending an arc equal to the radius|arc length equals radius
Solution: One radian is the central angle subtending an arc whose length equals the radius. In theta=s/r, setting s=r gives theta=1 radian. Both lengths must use the same unit.

Question Choices: Write radian measure theta as a ratio of arc length s to radius r.
Solution: Radian measure is the dimensionless ratio theta=s/r, arc length divided by the positive radius. Rearranging gives s=r*theta; use the same units for the two lengths.

Question Choices: Find the arc length when r=12 and theta=pi/3 radians in terms of pi.
Solution: The angle is in radians, so s=r*theta=12*(pi/3)=4*pi length units. Do not use the sector-area formula, which has squared radius.

Question Choices: What radian measure represents one complete revolution?
Hints: A half turn is pi radians.|Double pi.
Solution: One complete revolution is 360 degrees. Multiply by pi/180 to get 2pi radians. A half revolution is pi radians.

Question Choices: An arc is 1/6 of a circumference. Find its central angle in radians.
Solution: A full turn is 2pi radians. The arc and central angle occupy the same fraction 1/6, so theta=(1/6)*2pi=1/3pi radians.
